title: write() zeroizes kbuf using count after partial copy_from_user
description: In crypto2dev_fd_write(), after copy_from_user fails the function returns -EFAULT immediately and calls kfree(kbuf) — correct. But on the success path (all other returns), the cleanup at 'out:' does memzero_explicit(kbuf, count) then kfree(kbuf). This is after the mutex_unlock but using 'count' (the user-requested size) not 'outlen'. That is fine for the kbuf itself. However: the function returns 'ret' (= count on success) via 'out:' path. The wake_up check 'if (ret > 0 && outlen > 0)' can be reached with outlen==0 (e.g. UNSET fd path where outlen is never set from its initial 0, yet ret==count>0). The wake_up is then skipped, which is correct for UNSET. But the same issue applies to OPERATION path where update() produced zero output bytes and outlen==0: wake_up is correctly skipped. No bug here on wake_up — recording as checked. REAL BUG: if the goto out path is taken from the UNSET branch (fd_type==UNSET), outlen remains 0 from its initializer; then 'memzero_explicit(kbuf, count)' runs after unlock — but kbuf still points to the kmalloc'd buffer, which is correct. ACTUAL CONFIRMED BUG: on the UNSET path, the inbuf_append() may fail (-ENOMEM or -EMSGSIZE). In that case ret<0 and kbuf is freed. But kbuf is memzero'd with 'count' bytes before kfree regardless of whether inbuf_append succeeded — this is correct zeroization behavior. No bug in write(). Closing this investigation — no issue found here.
